title: Check Around and Find Out: Permit the Promotion
summary: Finish the rook check, then use the king to protect a mating bishop square even while White promotes.

nodes.question: When should Black stop checking and let White promote?
nodes.explanation: Rc1+ forces Kb8, after which Ka6 protects a7. White can promote a pawn, but cannot stop the protected adjacent bishop check.

branches.title: Source finish: allow a queen
commentary: Begin from the saved later Kc8 diagram. White still has Ba8 and pawns on b7, d7, f7 and h7; none is removed to reduce the piece count.
Rc1+ checks along the c-file. The bishop on b6 covers d8, so White cannot step back to that square.
Kb8 is the only legal reply. The b7 pawn and bishop on a8 occupy the other nearby squares, while the rook controls the c-file.
Ka6 is the quiet source move. It protects a7, so the next bishop check cannot be answered by Kxa7. Black can finally allow a promotion.
d8=Q follows the source and creates a queen, but the new queen has no way to capture the bishop on a7 or block its adjacent diagonal check.
Ba7# checks Kb8. Ka6 protects a7 and b7, Rc1 covers c8/c7, and White’s own bishop fills a8. Promotion has not opened an escape.
branches.explanation: Ba7# checks Kb8. Ka6 protects a7 and b7, Rc1 covers c8/c7, and White’s own bishop fills a8. Promotion has not opened an escape.

branches.title: Independent defense: promote to a knight
commentary: Test a different promotion type with the complete board retained. This is an independent alternative to the source queen promotion.
Rc1+ forces the white king away from c8.
Kb8 enters the same cage formed by the rook, bishop and White’s own pieces.
Ka6 protects a7 before bringing the bishop there.
f8=N is legal and gives no check. The knight on f8 cannot capture a7 or answer a bishop check against the adjacent king.
Ba7# is actual mate. The finite certificate also checks queen, rook, bishop and knight promotions on d8, f8 and h8.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Ba7# is actual mate. The finite certificate also checks queen, rook, bishop and knight promotions on d8, f8 and h8.

branches.title: Independent defense: promote the h-pawn
commentary: Test the most distant new queen instead of assuming all promotion squares are equivalent.
Rc1+ keeps White from spending this move on promotion.
Kb8 is forced by the complete legal-move list.
Ka6 supplies the king support that makes the next bishop check decisive.
h8=Q creates a queen along the eighth rank, but Ba8 blocks its line to a8 and no queen move can interrupt an adjacent bishop check.
Ba7# leaves no legal king move, capture or interposition. The full nine-piece mating position is preserved.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Ba7# leaves no legal king move, capture or interposition. The full nine-piece mating position is preserved.

exercises.prompt: Why is Ka6 necessary before Ba7?
exercises.answer: Ka6 protects a7. After the bishop checks from a7, the white king cannot capture it.

exercises.prompt: How many promotion replies are checked after Ka6?
exercises.answer: Twelve: queen, rook, bishop and knight promotions on d8, f8 and h8. The b7 pawn is blocked by its own king, and Ba8 is blocked by b7.

startContext: Begin after Kc8 at 86 seconds in the complete nine-piece later diagram. Rc1+/Kb8/Ka6 is proved against all twelve White promotions, each met by actual Ba7 mate; the white bishop and all four seventh-rank pawns are preserved. d8=Q is illustrated by the source; f8=N and h8=Q are explicitly independent comparison defenses. This finite legal mate proof does not certify the earlier long bishop-and-rook shepherd, premature promotion interpositions or claims of a forced route from the original board.
